claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially exists as a high-temperature disordered BCC phase.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between the thermodynamic driving force for Al partitioning and kinetic limitations on Al diffusion during cooling.
At high temperature, configurational entropy stabilizes the disordered BCC phase.
Cooling reduces the entropy contribution to free energy relative to the enthalpic benefit of chemical ordering.
Cooling creates a thermodynamic incentive for Al segregation and associated short-range ordering.
Al partitioning leads to chemical ordering and phase separation.
Slow cooling permits sufficient Al diffusion to form chemically enriched regions.
Al-enriched regions trigger transformation toward a more thermodynamically stable, chemically segregated state.
Local Al segregation and ordered clusters, potentially B2-type, promote nucleation of secondary phases distinct from the high-temperature BCC structure.
Fast cooling suppresses diffusion and retains a metastable BCC structure.
Slowly cooled samples will show more secondary-phase formation and/or chemical ordering than rapidly quenched samples.
Rapidly quenched samples will largely retain the high-temperature BCC phase.
A rapid-quench sample and a slow-cooled sample should be compared while composition, starting temperature, and atmosphere are held constant.
Cooling from approximately 1050°C to room temperature spans the onset of significant Al mobility in this alloy.
The rapid-quench sample serves as the baseline because quenching minimizes atomic diffusion and preserves the initial BCC structure.
The proposed mechanism applies in the temperature regime where Al diffusion is appreciable.
The cooling-rate effect should diminish beyond a threshold at which diffusion is effectively suppressed.
XRD, TEM, and EDS can respectively assess phase or ordering peaks, ordered domains or precipitates, and spatial variation in Al concentration.
The hypothesis would be falsified if slow-cooled and quenched samples showed no detectable difference in phase composition, chemical ordering, or Al segregation.
